narrative.overview:
The logo is an ink-black owl with a red eye, beside a route line that ends in a red pin. The app takes its two jobs from it. Ink is the hand that writes the record: every action, every selected state, every line of text someone acts on. Red is the eye on the route: it marks where a passenger boards and where they get off, and nothing else. The ledger part is the discipline: figures line up, each status is stated in a word, and nothing shows a fact the system does not have.

The app is clean and minimal, built to be read in sunlight at a van door. Paper-grey screens with white cards, one ink action per decision, status said in words on a tinted chip. It is calm and exact rather than expressive. Weight, spacing and alignment carry the hierarchy. The interface stays quiet, so a warning or an SOS stands out the moment it appears. Light theme only; the app has no dark theme.

The September purple (`#2D2059`) is retired. Anything still purple, or anything that describes a "purple brand", is out of date.
keyCharacteristics: Ink (`#16161D`) does every action. Red marks route geometry only.
Status is a meaning (`StatusTone`), never a loose colour, and always comes with a word or an icon.
Every colour pair is measured against WCAG 2.1 AA; control edges clear 3:1.
Roboto bundled at 400 / 500 / 700, so type is identical on every phone.
Full-width 52 px primary actions, 48 px minimum targets, one-handed reach.
Flat by default; soft ambient shadows only on raised cards.

rules.name: The One Meaning for Red Rule
rules.body: Pin Red marks route geometry and is never a button fill. On an action, red means stop or danger, and that is SOS Red. A red Book beside a red Cancel beside a red SOS would make all three look equally alarming.

rules.name: The Pair Rule
rules.body: A status colour is chosen as a `StatusTone`, which hands over its text colour and container together, both verified. Never pick a foreground on its own, and never let hue alone carry the status: the label or an icon goes with it.

rules.name: The Edge Rule
rules.body: If a user must locate it to operate it, its boundary is Control Edge (3:1 or more). Hairline is for decoration, where nothing needs to be found.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Every peso amount goes through `Money`, with tabular figures, so a fare that changes never makes its column jump. Lists that are scanned show whole pesos (₱1,180); receipts show centavos (₱1,180.00).

rules.name: The Uncapped Rule
rules.body: No text size is capped and no single-line height is hardcoded. Text must survive 200 % system scaling (WCAG 1.4.4), which is why headline sizes stay restrained.

rules.name: The Carried Type Rule
rules.body: The family is bundled, never fetched and never borrowed from the phone. The app is used in connectivity dead zones, and a font that arrives over the network is missing exactly when it matters.

rules.name: The Whisper Shadow Rule
rules.body: A card shadow is black at 5 % or less, 8 to 15 px blur, 4 to 5 px offset. No hard, coloured or stacked shadows. Map markers are the only stronger ones.

rules.name: The Border or Shadow Rule
rules.body: A card has a Hairline outline (outlined card) or a soft shadow (raised card), not both.

dos: **Do** take every colour from `AppColors` or the theme, and every status colour through `StatusTone`.
**Do** state a status in words (Label Small capitals) or with an icon, never by colour alone.
**Do** make the primary action an Owl Ink slab, full width, 52 px tall, within thumb reach.
**Do** keep every tappable target at 48 × 48 px or more.
**Do** outline every control a user must find in Control Edge (3:1 or more).
**Do** route every peso amount through `Money` (tabular figures).
**Do** start titles and content on the 16 px gutter, titles left-aligned.
**Do** keep motion at 100 / 180 / 240 ms and honour reduce motion.
donts: **Don't** fill a button with Pin Red, or use Pin Red for anything other than route geometry.
**Don't** bring back the retired purple (`#2D2059`) or a coloured app bar.
**Don't** write raw `Colors.*` or `Color(0x…)` in a screen. About 40 such uses remain in the profile, messages and notification screens; they are drift, not precedent.
**Don't** use amber or yellow as text; it fails on white. Use Ochre.
**Don't** give a card both an outline and a shadow, or a shadow heavier than 5 % black.
**Don't** centre an app bar title or hide navigation labels.
**Don't** fetch a font at runtime or cap text size.
